headline: No cool break on the chart — Thursday the calmer scout
body:
Weather first. Wednesday inside the channel is easy: light morning air turning SW/W 5–10 kt, seas 2–3 ft, and the triangle itself runs about 2.9 ft on 8–11 kt WNW. Fine water. The rough part is offshore — Santa Rosa Flats sits above 4 ft on 11–13 kt NW, and stays that way both days. Thursday inside is softer still, near-glass early (3–5 kt) and 2.8 ft at the triangle, but mind patchy fog and a hard NW build Thursday night. No advisory in hand; treat the outer zones as the hazard.

Now the honest call. Nothing on the chart is holding the 64–68 band. Every triangle corner reads warm — west 73.8, east 73.3, south point 72.0 — with the coolest trend toward the south point over Santa Cruz Basin. The break isn't inside the triangle, and it hasn't slid to a nearer ground. Farthest and coolest is San Nicolas at 69.7, still a notch above the red 68 line. Neither day is a true break day. If you must scout, take Thursday's calm and work that south edge for bait.
